FELUCCA CHIP VR

Felucca with two new chip engines: 2A03, the NES's channels, and OPN2, Genesis-style four-operator FM. The firmware is compiled from source and laid out on six panels in an 8-bit world, where the hills are an equalizer and every note leaves a pixel behind. One panel reads your hands from a webcam or a Quest's hand tracking; the sequencer has its own, behind you.

HOW TO PLAY
The sound
Track 1 starts on the 2A03's pulse lead, track 2 on its triangle bass, track 3 on OPN2's E.PIANO and track 4 on the 2A03's drum kit. In PRESETS the two new engines come first.
2A03
CHAN picks the channel: PLS, TRI, NOIS, P+T (pulse over a triangle an octave down), DUAL (two detuned pulses) or KIT (drums on the keys). DUTY has the chip's four widths plus BITE and WAH sequences; ENV is the chip's envelope; SWP is its pitch sweep.
OPN2
VOIC picks one of 12 patches (bass, piano, brass, bell, strings, lead, guitar, organ and more). ALG, FB, MLVL and MEG change it, and CHIP picks the console: MD1 (gritty and dark), MD2, or 3438 (clean).
Mallets
Each controller holds a mallet. Tap keys and buttons with the ball.
Trigger
Point and pull to press a key or button. On a knob, hold the trigger and twist your wrist.
Grip
Point at a panel, squeeze the grip and move it anywhere. The layout is remembered.
Thumbstick
Point at a knob and push up or down to turn it.
Sequencer
Behind you (turn round; on the desktop press SEQUENCER ↻ or `). The top strip is all 64 steps of the selected track, the page below 16 of them as a piano roll (or the eight drum lanes: VIEW), with each step's velocity under it. Tap the roll to put a note in; tap it again once its step is selected to take it out. The two rows of buttons edit the selected step: TIME (note, tie, rest), NOTE and OCT, ACCENT, SLIDE, RATCH (x1 to x4), VEL, CHANCE (percent, then the 1:2 to !FILL conditions), NUDGE, CLEAR, COPY and PASTE, and the track's LEN, DIV, SWING and GATE. KEY and SCALE drop down a choice of 12 keys and 16 scales; the roll then tints the scale's rows (the root strongest) and marks notes outside it with a black notch. ENTER writes the keys you play into the selected step and moves on. UNDO takes back the panel's edits. FOLLOW keeps the page on the playing step. SAVE on FUNCTION keeps the pattern, as on the FM-1.
Tracking
START TRACKING turns on the webcam (or, in the headset, the Quest's own hand tracking) and the fifth panel shows what it sees. THEREMIN: your playing hand's height aims at a key; pinch thumb and finger to start a note, and keep pinching while you move: it stays one note and the pitch follows you (PITCH picks a smooth SLIDE, or STEPS, WHITE or OCTAVE that snap to keys); pinch with the other hand and slide up or down for volume. KNOBS: the frame is split into the eight knobs; pinch over one and twist your wrist to turn it; let go and grab again for more. GESTURES: hold an open palm for PLAY/STOP, a V sign for the next track, swipe sideways for presets and up or down for octaves. The camera stays in this browser; nothing is uploaded. The claude.ai preview blocks cameras, so download the page and open the file to use a webcam.
Zoom, move
Desktop: click a panel's frame (not a key or knob) to fly straight onto it, filling the window; double-click empty space to go back. The wheel zooms toward the pointer. Shift + drag a panel to move it (it turns to face you); Shift + wheel over it pushes it away or pulls it closer. Headset: point at a panel and squeeze the grip to carry it; lean in to look closer. RESET PANELS puts everything back.
Desktop
Click keys and buttons, drag knobs up or down, drag empty space to look around. Z–' and Q–O play keys, 1–= are FX … REC, [ ] OCT, arrows turn SELECT and ALGORITHM (which picks the track). Esc hides or shows this card.

Lower the intensity if the motion is uncomfortable. Felucca by Leo Kuroshita, Hügelton Instruments (GPL-3.0 source); the 2A03 and OPN2 engines were written for this build. Not affiliated with M-VAVE, Nintendo, Sega or Yamaha.
